ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.claim: Those who reject resurrection will find their confession useless; belief after seeing the realities would negate the purpose of intellect and moral awareness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r3.anchor: a confession of sins by people will be of no avail to them on that day.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r8.claim: God commands the Messenger to state the summary: their souls will be taken, then they will return to their Lord's recompense through resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r8.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى أن يخبرهم بجملة الحال غير مفصلة، من قبض أرواحهم، ثم عودهم إلى جزاء ربهم بالبعث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r9.claim: The Angel of Death is named Azrael, meaning servant of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r9.anchor: وملك الموت: اسمه عزرائيل، ومعناه عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r10.claim: The majority read ترجعون in the passive; Zayd ibn Ali reads it in the active.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p434/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ترجعون، مبنيا للمفعول وزيد بن علي: مبنيا للفاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r1.claim: A cited poem uses the verb for being fully counted, supporting the sense of God taking people completely at death.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r2.claim: The Angel of Death is named ʿAzrāʾīl, and all his actions occur by God’s command and creation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r2.anchor: وملك الموت اسمه عزرائيل وتصرفه كله بأمر الله وبخلقه واختراعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r3.claim: A report says God takes the spirits of all animals without the Angel of Death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r3.anchor: وروي في الحديث أن البهائم كلها يتوفى الله روحها دون ملك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this means God extinguishes animals’ life; the same applies to humans, but their souls are taken through an angel and attendant angels as an honor, and this intensifies the disbelievers’ punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r4.anchor: وكذلك الأمر في بني آدم إلا أنه نوع شرف بتصرف ملك وملائكة معه في قبض أرواحهم، وكذلك أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r5.claim: Mujāhid compares the world in the Angel of Death’s hands to a basin in a person’s hands: he takes souls from wherever commanded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p360/r5.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد: أن الدنيا بين يدي ملك الموت كالطست بين يدي الإنسان

MAJAZ:v2p131/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p131/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p131/r5.claim: Yatawaffākum is related to counting the dead; Manẓūr al-Zubayrī's line says Quraysh did not count them among the total.
MAJAZ:v2p131/r5.anchor: مجازه من: توفى العدد من الموتى.

MAJAZ:v2p131/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p131/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p131/r6.claim: Manẓūr al-Zubayrī uses tawaffā for counting people in the phrase that Quraysh did not count them among the number.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r4.claim: The verse's wording indicates that the Angel of Death is a specific angel assigned to take souls.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r4.anchor: الظاهر من هذه الآية أن ملك الموت شخص معين من الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r5.speaker: قتادة وغير واحد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r5.claim: Some reports, including Qatada's, call the Angel of Death Azrael, the commonly known name; he has assistants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r5.anchor: وقد سمي في بعض الآثار بعزرائيل، وهو المشهور، قاله قتادة وغير واحد، وله أعوان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r6.claim: A hadith says the Angel of Death's assistants draw souls from the body, then the Angel of Death takes them when they reach the throat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r6.anchor: ورد في الحديث أن أعوانه ينتزعون الأرواح من سائر الجسد، حتى إذا بلغت الحلقوم تناولها ملك الموت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, so he can take souls from wherever he wishes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد: حويت له الأرض فجعلت له مثل الطست

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r8.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad relays a similar account from the Prophet as a mursal report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r8.anchor: ورواه زهير بن محمد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، بنحوه مرسلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas also transmits the account that the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r9.anchor: وقالَه ابن عباس، رضي الله عنهما.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r10.claim: In a report from Ja'far ibn Muhammad's father, the Prophet asks the Angel of Death to treat a believing companion gently; the angel says he is gentle to every believer, inspects every home five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito's soul without God's command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r10.anchor: فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يا ملك الموت، ارفق بصاحبي فإنه مؤمن". فقال ملك الموت: يا محمد، طب نفسا وقر عينا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r11.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r11.claim: Ja'far says the Angel of Death inspects people at prayer times; when a person who kept prayer is dying, the angel approaches, repels Satan, and prompts the testimony of faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p360#2/r11.anchor: قال جعفر: بلغني أنه إنما يتصفحهم عند

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Angel of Death visits every house, whether tent or masonry, twice each day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r1.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: حدثنا محمد بن مسلم، عن إبراهيم بن ميسرة قال: سمعت مجاهدا يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r2.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r2.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the Angel of Death stands at the door of every inhabited house seven times daily, checking whether anyone there is due to die.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r2.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والله ما من بيت فيه أحد من أهل الدنيا إلا وملك الموت يقوم على بابه كل يوم سبع مرات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r3.claim: Returning to the Lord means resurrection from the graves on the appointed day for recompense.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p361/r3.anchor: يوم معادكم وقيامكم من قبوركم لجزائكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r9.claim: The Angel of Death takes people’s souls; tawaffī means taking something in full, like collecting a number or debt in full.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r9.anchor: أي يقبض أرواحكم والتوفي أخذ الشيء على تمام , مأخوذ من توفية العدد ومنه قولهم استوفيت ديني من فلان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r10.claim: The commentary gives two views on whether the Angel of Death takes souls with assistants or by himself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r10.anchor: ثم في توفي ملك الموت لهم قولان : الأول : بأعوانه . الثاني : بنفسه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r11.speaker: جعفر الصادق عن أبيه
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r11.claim: In a report from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq through his father, the Prophet asks the Angel of Death to treat a believing Anṣārī gently; the angel says he is gentle with every believer, surveys every household five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito without God’s command. Jaʿfar says these visits occur at prayer times.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r11.anchor: روى جعفر الصادق عن أبيه قال نظر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r12.claim: Returning to God means returning to His recompense, or reaching a state where none but God can cause benefit or harm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p356/r12.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : إلى جزائه . الثاني : إلى أن لا يملك لكم أحد ضرا ولا نفعا إلا الله

MUQATIL:32:10-11/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:10-11/r4.speaker: they
MUQATIL:32:10-11/r4.claim: Muqatil reports the claim that the Angel of Death is named Azrael and describes him as spanning the world, with four wings and a body between heaven and earth.
MUQATIL:32:10-11/r4.anchor: يزعمون أن اسمه عزرائيل، وله أربعة أجنحة جناح بالمشرق، وجناح بالمغرب،

MUQATIL:32:10-11/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:10-11/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:32:10-11/r5.claim: After death, people return alive to their Lord, who recompenses them according to their deeds.

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.claim: The first half treats revelation, God, creation especially of human beings, and Resurrection and Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r13.anchor: The first half of the sūrah discusses revelation (vv. 2–3), God (vv. 4–6), creation,

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r3.claim: Tawaffī means taking something completely, as when a debt is collected in full.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r3.anchor: توفي الشيء أخذه تاما كاملا كتوفي الحق وتوفي الدين من المديون.

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r4.claim: A reported gloss takes the assigned angel as charged with causing death and taking souls, but the verse's unrestricted wording appears broader.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r4.anchor: قيل أي وكل بإماتتكم وقبض أرواحكم والآية مطلقة ظاهرة في أعم من ذلك.

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r5.claim: The Qur'an attributes taking souls to God, the angel of death, and the angelic messengers because they occupy different levels in the causal hierarchy.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r5.anchor: وقد نسب التوفي في الآية إلى ملك الموت، وفي قوله والله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r6.claim: The messengers are the angel of death's assistants; he executes God's command, while God is the ultimate cause behind all causes.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r6.anchor: فالسبب القريب الملائكة الرسل أعوان ملك الموت وفوقهم ملك الموت الآمر بذلك المجري لأمر الله

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r7.claim: The layered attribution resembles writing: the pen, hand, and person can each be called a writer.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r7.anchor: فذلك بوجه كمثل كتابة الإنسان بالقلم فالقلم كاتب واليد كاتبة والإنسان كاتب.

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r8.claim: The return to God is the meeting mentioned in the prior verse, namely resurrection after death; ثم marks its temporal delay after death.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r8.anchor: هو الرجوع الذي عبر عنه في الآية السابقة باللقاء وموطنه البعث المترتب على التوفي والمتراخي عنه

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r10.claim: Death is not human annihilation: the angel takes the complete self from the body, while only bodies decay; the self remains preserved until God restores it to its body for judgment and recompense.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r10.anchor: بل ملك الموت الموكل بكم يأخذكم تامين كاملين من أجسادكم أي ينزع أرواحكم من أبدانكم

TABATABAI:32:10-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r11.claim: The human essence is the self referred to by “I,” distinct from and primary over the body; it does not perish at death, so bodily dissolution does not eliminate the person.
TABATABAI:32:10-11/r11.anchor: وهي لا تتلاشى بالموت ولا تنعدم بل محفوظة في قدرة الله حتى يؤذن في رجوعها

TABATABAI:32:1-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:1-14/r1.speaker: ملك الموت
TABATABAI:32:1-14/r1.claim: In a report about the Prophet visiting an Anṣārī, the angel says he is gentle with every believer, encounters every household five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito's soul without God's command.
TABATABAI:32:1-14/r1.anchor: فإذا ملك الموت عند رأسه فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يا ملك الموت ارفق بصاحبي

THALABI:v7p327/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p327/r15.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p327/r15.claim: Mujāhid says the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a tray, allowing him to take from wherever he wished.
THALABI:v7p327/r15.anchor: قال مجاهد: حويت له الأرض فجعلت له مثل طست يتناول منها حيث يشاء

THALABI:v7p327/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p327/r16.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v7p327/r16.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī report that the Angel of Death is named ʿAzrāʾīl, has four wings, spans the world with his legs, and can take souls everywhere as if the world were in his palm; he is aided by angels of mercy and punishment.
THALABI:v7p327/r16.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: بلغنا أن اسم ملك الموت عزرائيل وله أربعة أجنحة: جناح له بالمشرق، وجناح له بالمغرب

THALABI:v7p328/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p328/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p328/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Angel of Death’s stride stretches from east to west.
THALABI:v7p328/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن خطوة ملك الموت ما بين المشرق والمغرب

THALABI:v7p328/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p328/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
THALABI:v7p328/r2.claim: Muʿādh b. Jabal says the Angel of Death carries a spear spanning east to west, examines people twice daily, and strikes those whose appointed time has ended, saying they now join the army of the dead.
THALABI:v7p328/r2.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال: إن لملك الموت حربة تبلغ ما بين المشرق والمغرب، وهو يتصفح وجوه الناس

THALABI:v7p328/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p328/r3.speaker: خيثمة وشهر بن حوشب
THALABI:v7p328/r3.claim: Khaythamah and Shahr b. Ḥawshab report that a man asked Solomon to send him to India by wind after seeing the Angel of Death; the angel then explained that he had been ordered to take the man’s soul there.
THALABI:v7p328/r3.anchor: عن خيثمة وعن شهر بن حوشب قال: دخل ملك الموت على سليمان، فجعل ينظر إلى رجل من جلسائه يديم إليه النظر

THALABI:v7p328/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p328/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p328/r4.claim: The angels’ taking of souls means grasping and drawing them out; the Angel of Death summons them, they answer, and he orders his aides to seize them, while God creates death.
THALABI:v7p328/r4.anchor: قيل: توفي الملائكة: القبض والنزع. وتوفي ملك الموت: الدعاء والأمر، يدعو الأرواح فتجيبه ثم يأمر أعوانه بقبضها، وتوفي الله سبحانه: خلق الموت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:10-14/r2.claim: The angel of death takes people's spirits; “takes you fully” means seizing your souls.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r4.claim: The Angel of Death takes their souls; the earth is like a platter from which he picks them up as a bird picks up grain.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r4.anchor: تفسير السدي قال: {ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم} [السجدة: 11] جعلت لملك الموت الأرض مثل الطست يقبض أرواحهم كما يلتقط الطير الحب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r5.claim: The earth was laid out for the Angel of Death like a platter, so he can reach whichever place he wishes.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r5.anchor: عاصم بن حكيم، أن مجاهدا قال: جونت له الأرض فجعلت مثل الطست ينال منها حيث يشاء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r6.claim: Yahya had received the report that the Angel of Death takes the spirit of every creature on land and sea.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r6.anchor: قال يحيى: وبلغنا أنه يقبض روح كل شيء في البر والبحر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r7.claim: Their return to God takes place on the Day of Resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p687/r7.anchor: ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون} [السجدة: 11] يوم القيامة.

RAZI-FULL:v25p154/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154/r3.claim: The next verse begins to describe what awaits them from death through punishment, following the account of their denial of resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154/r3.anchor: ثم بين ما يكون لهم من الموت إلى العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r1.claim: The return to God entails that death must be followed by life.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r1.anchor: يعني لا بد من الموت ثم من الحياة بعده

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r2.claim: The angel's being entrusted with them means he does not neglect them or delay their death when their appointed term arrives; this is his sole task.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه لا يغفل عنكم وإذا جاء أجلكم لا يؤخركم

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r3.claim: Tawaffī means taking or receiving in full, and qabḍ means grasping; absolute annihilation is not a taking, so the verse indicates souls remain.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r3.anchor: فإن التوفي الاستيفاء والقبض هو الأخذ والإعدام المحض ليس بأخذ

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r4.claim: Pure souls remain with angels like a person among congenial family, increasing in clarity and strength; wicked souls are like prisoners among strangers, dwindling in strength and worsening in misery and opacity.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r4.anchor: ثم إن الروح الزكي الطاهر يبقى عند الملائكة مثل الشخص بين أهله

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r5.speaker: الحكماء
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r5.claim: The philosophers say pure souls attach to a heavenly body better than their former body and perfect themselves through it, while wicked souls gain no perfection after the second attachment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r5.anchor: والحكماء يقولون إن الأرواح الطاهرة تتعلق بجسم سماوي خير من بدنها

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r6.claim: Razi agrees with the philosophers if this is what they mean; otherwise their account may be true or false depending on their intended meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r6.anchor: فإن أرادوا ما ذكر بها فقد وافقونا وإلا فيغير النظر في ذلك بحسب إرادتهم فقد يكون قولهم حقا

RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r7.claim: Mentioning death answers denial of revival: the angel takes the soul while bodily parts disperse, so gathering them and having the angel return what he took present no difficulty; the souls are preserved for their bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v25p154#2/r7.anchor: الملك يقبض الروح والأجزاء تتفرق فجمع الأجزاء لا بعد فيه

STUDYQURAN:32:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r1.claim: Islamic angelology identifies the Angel of Death as Azrael, who removes spirits from bodies at death.
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r1.anchor: the Angel of death is understood to be Azrael (IK, Q), who is in charge of removing spirits from bodies

STUDYQURAN:32:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r2.claim: The Angel of Death is said to have angelic helpers in taking souls, while another verse says God takes souls at death.
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r2.anchor: he is said to have helpers among the angels (IK, Ṭ; see 4:97c; 8:50; 16:32), though it is also said that God takes souls

STUDYQURAN:32:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r3.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reconciles the accounts: the Angel of Death seizes souls, helping angels attend them, and God brings about their end.
STUDYQURAN:32:11/r3.anchor: Al-Qurṭubī reconciles these verses by saying that the Angel of Death seizes them

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r1.claim: The command states the truth and refutes the disbelievers' false claim.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r1.anchor: بيانا للحق وردا على زعمهم الباطل

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r2.claim: Tawaffī means taking something fully and completely, including completing a count.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r2.anchor: التوفي أخذ الشيء تاما وافيا واستيفاء العدد

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r3.speaker: الصحاح
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ says tawaffāhu Allāh means God took his spirit, and wafāh means death.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r3.anchor: قال في "الصحاح" توفاه الله قبض روحه والوفاة الموت

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r4.claim: An angel is a subtle, luminous body able to assume different forms.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r4.anchor: والملك جسم لطيف نوراني يتشكل بأشكال مختلفة

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r5.speaker: بعض المحققين
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r5.claim: Some investigators distinguish an angel entrusted with administration from a human ruler; the administrative angels include the Angel of Death.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r5.anchor: قال بعض المحققين : المتولي من الملائكة شيئا من السياسة يقال له ملك بالفتح

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r6.claim: Death is an existing quality created as the opposite of life.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r6.anchor: والموت صفة وجودية خلقت ضدا للحياة

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r7.claim: ʿAzrāʾīl takes souls fully by severe means, including striking faces and backs; alternatively, the verse stresses that no one whose time has come is left behind.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى يقبض عزرائيل أرواحكم بحيث لا يترك منها شيئا بل يستوفيها ويأخذها تماما على أشد ما يكون

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r8.claim: A report says that after all creatures die, God tells the sole remaining Angel of Death that his turn has come and orders him to lie between Paradise and Hell and die.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r8.anchor: يقول الله لملك الموت من بقي من خلقي وهو أعلم

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r9.claim: The verse rejects the view that death is only a natural condition arising accidentally from an animal's constitution.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r9.anchor: وفي الآية رد للكافرين حيث زعموا أن الموت من الأحوال الطبيعية العارضة للحيوان بموجب الجبلة

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r10.claim: Tawkīl means relying on another, making them a deputy, and entrusting them with a task.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r10.anchor: التوكيل أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r11.claim: The angel is entrusted with taking souls and recording appointed lifespans.

BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r12.claim: Returning to the Lord means resurrection for reckoning and recompense, the meaning of meeting God.
BURSEVI:v7p85#2/r12.anchor: تردون بالبعث للحساب والجزاء وهذا معنى لقاء الله

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r1.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq calls death repentance, citing the command to repent to the Maker and kill yourselves: the repentant has killed himself.
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r1.anchor: قال الإمام جعفر بن محمد الصادق رضي الله عنه : الموت هو التوبة قال تعالى : {فتوبوا إلى بارئكم فاقتلوا أنفسكم}

BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r2.claim: A Persian couplet urges washing away error before one is suddenly bound and carried off.
BURSEVI:v7p86#3/r2.anchor: مكن دامن ازكرد زلت بشوى كه ناكه زبالا به بندند وى

TAB-FULL:v18p604/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r1.claim: The Angel of Death takes your souls and thereby completes your number; a rajaz line uses the same verb in a numerical sense.

TAB-FULL:v18p604/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Angel of Death is accompanied by helper angels.
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم} [السجدة: 11] قال: ملك الموت يتوفاكم، ومعه أعوان من الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v18p604/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the earth is gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, from which he takes wherever he wishes.
TAB-FULL:v18p604/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: قوله " {يتوفاكم ملك الموت} [السجدة: 11] قال: حويت له الأرض، فجعلت له مثل الطست، يتناول منها حيث يشاء

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r1.claim: The death angel's taking of souls answers the deniers' question about being lost in the earth and resolves their objection; treating tawaffī as generic death misses the wording's point.
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r1.anchor: وظهر بما تقدم أولا وجه اتصال قوله

TABATABAI:32:11-13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r2.claim: The verse is among the clearest Qur'anic proofs that the soul is immaterial, distinct from the body and its states.
TABATABAI:32:11-13/r2.anchor: أن الآية من أوضح الآيات القرآنية الدالة على تجرد النفس بمعنى كونها غير البدن أو شيء من حالات البدن

TABRISI:32:12/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r1.speaker: الراجز
TABRISI:32:12/r1.claim: The author defines tawaffī as taking something fully and cites a rajaz line whose “they did not take them” witnesses the verb.
TABRISI:32:12/r1.anchor: اللغة: التوفي أخذ الشيء على تمام قال الراجز: إن بني دارم ليسوا من أحد ولا توفتهم قريش في العدد

TABRISI:32:12/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r2.claim: Istīfāʾ of a debt means taking it in full.
TABRISI:32:12/r2.anchor: يقال: استوفى الدين إذا قبضه على كماله

TABRISI:32:12/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r3.claim: Tawkīl means entrusting an affair to another to carry it out.
TABRISI:32:12/r3.anchor: والتوكيل تفويض الأمر إلى غيره للقيام به

TABRISI:32:12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r9.claim: The Prophet is told to say that the Angel of Death takes all of them, meaning he takes each person until none remain.
TABRISI:32:12/r9.anchor: أي يقبض أرواحكم أجمعين. وقيل: يقبضكم واحدا واحدا

TABRISI:32:12/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:32:12/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the world is placed before the Angel of Death like a bowl from which he takes at will without effort, with a stride spanning east to west.
TABRISI:32:12/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: جعلت الدنيا بين يدي ملك الموت مثل جام يأخذ منها ما شاء إذا قضى عليه الموت

TABRISI:32:12/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r11.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
TABRISI:32:12/r11.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi say the Angel of Death has many helpers, angels of mercy and angels of punishment.
TABRISI:32:12/r11.anchor: إن له أعوانا كثيرة من ملائكة الرحمة وملائكة العذاب عن قتادة والكلبي

TABRISI:32:12/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r12.claim: On that view, “the Angel of Death” is a collective designation, as verses also ascribe taking souls to messengers and angels.
TABRISI:32:12/r12.anchor: فعلى هذا المراد بملك الموت الجنس ويدل عليه قوله

TABRISI:32:12/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r13.claim: Taking souls is attributed to God because He created death and no one else can control it.
TABRISI:32:12/r13.anchor: فلأنها سبحانه خلق الموت ولا يقدر عليه أحد سواه

TABRISI:32:12/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:12/r14.claim: Returning to God means being brought to His recompense of reward or punishment; calling it a return to Him magnifies the matter.
TABRISI:32:12/r14.anchor: ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون } أي إلى جزاء ربكم من الثواب والعقاب

TABRISI:32:12/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:12/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:32:12/r15.claim: Ikrima transmits from Ibn Abbas the Prophet's account that illness and pain warn of death; when the term arrives, the Angel of Death comes as the final messenger, says he did not wrong the dead person's term or provision, and will return until none remain.
TABRISI:32:12/r15.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس. قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq explains that the Angel of Death takes all your souls without leaving anyone out, like fully collecting what is owed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: تأويله أنه يقبض أرواحكم أجمعين، فلا ينقص واحد منكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Angel of Death was charged with taking your souls.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد وكل بقبض أرواحكم (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r3.claim: Muqatil says that after death people return alive to their Lord, who requites them for their deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p144/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: يريد بعد الموت تصيرون إليه أحياء، فيجزيكم بأعمالكم (¬7).

QASHANI:32:11-12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:32:11-12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:32:11-12/r1.claim: The Angel of Death is the universal human soul, which receives partial souls that retain primordial nature and have not reached total corruption; souls that do reach that limit are separated by the angels of punishment.
QASHANI:32:11-12/r1.anchor: النفس الإنسانية الكلية التي هي معاد النفوس الجزئية ما لم تسقط عن الفطرة بالكلية وإن احتجبت الهيئات الظلمانية والصفات النفسانية

ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.claim: Elmalılı raises how this verse’s attribution of taking souls to God relates to the earlier statements that the Angel of Death and God’s envoys take them; the excerpt ends before his answer.
ELMALILI:39:42-52/r14.anchor: ٱلْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمْ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r1.claim: This verse and hadith literature call the angel charged with taking people’s lives the Angel of Death; Judaism and Christianity also teach that an angel or angels are assigned this task.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r1.anchor: insanların canını almakla görevlendirilen melekten ölüm meleği diye söz edilmektedir. Bu kavram ve Tanrı tarafından ölümü gerçekleştirmek üzere melek veya meleklerin görevlendirildiği inancı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r2.claim: Rabbinic works give more than ten names for the Angel of Death, including Azrael; Muslims commonly call him Azrāil, a probably Hebrew name absent from the Qur’an and sound hadith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r2.anchor: Rabbilere (yahudi din bilginlerine) ait eserlerde ondan fazla ölüm meleği adı yer alır ki bunlardan biri Azrael’dir. İslâmî literatürde ve müslümanlar arasında da ölüm meleğinin Azrâil adıyla anılması yaygınlık kazanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r3.claim: The verse uses a singular form for the death angel while other verses use plural malāʾika; this may mean Azrāil leads the angel group or has angelic helpers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r3.anchor: Buradan hareketle bu âyette geçen ve Azrâil olarak bilinen meleğin ruhları almakla görevli melekler topluluğunun reisi olduğunu veya meleklerden yardımcılarının bulunduğunu söylemek mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r4.claim: Other verses depict angels greeting protected believers as they take their souls, but striking and speaking harshly to those who wronged themselves through evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r4.anchor: Bazı âyetlerde, ölüm meleklerinin kötülüklerden korunan müminlerin ruhlarını kabzederken şefkat ve merhametle davranıp kendilerine selâm verdikleri (Nahl 16/32), kötülüklere saplanarak kendilerine zulmedenlerin canlarını alırken ise yüzlerine ve arkalarına vurarak onlara karşı sert ifadeler kullandıkları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r5.claim: Stories that Azrāil is colossal, has countless limbs, faces, eyes and tongues, or reads a person’s name from a leaf forty days before death lack Qur’anic or sound-hadith basis and derive from Isrāʾīliyyāt circulated by Jewish converts under Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:11/r5.anchor: bu tür hurafeler Hz. Ebû Bekir ve Ömer dönemlerinde müslüman olan bazı yahudi mühtedilerin rivayet ettikleri İsrâiliyat türünden haberlere dayanmaktadır

BURHAN:v2p64/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p64/r1.speaker: البغوي
BURHAN:v2p64/r1.claim: Al-Baghawi reconciles the verses: angels seize and extract souls, the Angel of Death summons them and orders his assistants to take them, and God creates death in them.
BURHAN:v2p64/r1.anchor: وجمع البغوي بينها لأن توفي الملائكة بالقبض والنزع وتوفي ملك الموت بالدعاء والأمر

ITQAN:v4p391/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p391/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p391/r8.claim: The name Azra'il is widely used for the Angel of Death; Abu al-Shaykh ibn Hibban transmits it from Wahb.
ITQAN:v4p391/r8.anchor: اشتهر على الألسنة أن اسمه عزرائيل ورواه أبو الشيخ بن حبان عن وهب

ITQAN:v1p128/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p128/r1.speaker: الشعبي
ITQAN:v1p128/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi reports that Israfil accompanied Muhammad’s prophethood for three years, teaching him words but not reciting the Quran; Gabriel then accompanied him for twenty years of Quranic revelation.
ITQAN:v1p128/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي قال أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم النبوة وهو ابن أربعين سنة

ITQAN:v1p128/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p128/r2.speaker: ابن عساكر
ITQAN:v1p128/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAsakir says Israfil’s charge over the Trumpet suits a prophethood heralding the Hour’s nearness and end of revelation; he gives comparable angelic assignments to Dhu al-Qarnayn and Khalid ibn Sinan.
ITQAN:v1p128/r2.anchor: قال ابن عساكر والحكمة في توكيل إسرافيل أنه الموكل بالصور

ITQAN:v1p128/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p128/r3.speaker: ابن سابط
ITQAN:v1p128/r3.claim: Ibn Sabit says three angels preserve what is in the Mother Book: Gabriel handles scriptures, revelation, wartime victory and destructive events; Michael rain and plants; the Angel of Death takes souls, and their records match at resurrection.
ITQAN:v1p128/r3.anchor: عن ابن سابط قال في أم الكتاب كل شيء هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

ITQAN:v1p128/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p128/r4.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
ITQAN:v1p128/r4.claim: ʿAta ibn al-Saʾib says Gabriel is first to be reckoned because he was God’s trustee over His messengers.
ITQAN:v1p128/r4.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب قال أول ما يحاسب جبريل لأنه كان أمين الله على رسله

ITQAN:v3p67/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r1.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
ITQAN:v3p67/r1.claim: Abu Musa recalls a surah like the Musabbihat they used to recite but later forgot, except for a verse warning believers against saying what they do not do.
ITQAN:v3p67/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال كنا نقرأ سورة نشبهها المسبحات

ITQAN:v3p67/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r2.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v3p67/r2.claim: Umar says they recited a warning against disowning their fathers as disbelief; Zayd ibn Thabit confirmed the wording when Umar asked him.
ITQAN:v3p67/r2.anchor: ثم قال لزيد بن ثابت أكذلك قال نعم

ITQAN:v3p67/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r3.speaker: عمر، عبد الرحمن بن عوف
ITQAN:v3p67/r3.claim: Umar asked ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf about a revealed command to strive as before; ʿAbd al-Rahman said it was among what had been dropped from the Quran.
ITQAN:v3p67/r3.anchor: قال عمر لعبد الرحمن بن عوف ألم تجد فيما أنزل علينا

ITQAN:v3p67/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r4.speaker: مسلمة بن مخلد الأنصاري
ITQAN:v3p67/r4.claim: Muslima ibn Mukhallad recited two passages absent from the codex, promising success to believers who emigrated and strove, and hidden delight as reward for those who sheltered, supported and defended them.
ITQAN:v3p67/r4.anchor: أن مسلمة بن مخلد الأنصاري قال لهم ذات يوم أخبروني بآيتين في القرآن لم يكتبا في المصحف

ITQAN:v3p67/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v3p67/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that two men who learned a surah from the Prophet could no longer recite a letter; the Prophet said it was among what had been abrogated and to leave it.
ITQAN:v3p67/r5.anchor: إن ابن عمر قال قرأ رجلان سورة أقرأهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v3p67/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r6.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v3p67/r6.claim: Anas reports that a passage about the Biʾr Maʿuna martyrs was recited until withdrawn: they told their people they had met their Lord, who was pleased with them and whom they pleased.
ITQAN:v3p67/r6.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أنس في قصة أصحاب بئر معونة الذين قتلوا

ITQAN:v3p67/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p67/r7.speaker: حذيفة
ITQAN:v3p67/r7.claim: Hudhayfa says the portion of the Quran people recite is only a quarter of Surat al-Tawba.
ITQAN:v3p67/r7.anchor: وفي المستدرك عن حذيفة قال ما تقرءون ربعها يعني براءة

DAMGHANI:v1p490/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r17.claim: Tawaffī can mean death: the angel of death takes the souls of people when they die.
DAMGHANI:v1p490/r17.anchor: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r1.claim: التوفي derives from completing or taking a number in full; to complete something is to exhaust it, as in related verb forms.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r1.anchor: التوفي : اسم مأخوذ من استيفاء العدد . واستيفاء الشيء : أن تستقضيه . يقال : توفيته ، واستوفيته .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r2.claim: Death is called الوفاة because it occurs when the lifespan has been completed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r2.anchor: والوفاة : اسم للموت ، لأنه يكون عند استيفاء العمر .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r4.claim: A second sense is taking souls in death, including the angel of death taking people and the angels taking the unjust or the virtuous.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن التوفي في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r6.speaker: أبو علي ابن البناء
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r6.claim: Ibn al-Banna transmits a scholar's account that the nafs leaves during sleep while spirit and life remain, enabling dreams, movement, and breathing; it returns instantly unless God keeps it and takes the spirit, causing death in sleep.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p213/r6.anchor: وحكى أبو علي ابن البناء من أصحابنا ، عن بعض أهل العلم أنه قال : للإنسان حياة وروح ونفس ، فإذا نام خرجت نفسه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r1.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r1.claim: Ali ibn Ubayd Allah considers the closest view to correct that the human nafs is a created spiritual substance of light, subtle and generally invisible; angels are likewise subtle bodies of light, while jinn and devils are made of fire.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : اختلف الناس في ماهية النفس المختصة بالآدمي اختلافا كثيرا . وأقربهم إلى الصواب قائلون قالوا : إنها جوهر روحاني

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r2.claim: One alternative view says the nafs is a subtle body.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r2.anchor: وقال قوم : إن النفس جسم لطيف .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r3.claim: Another view identifies the nafs with blood.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r4.claim: Another view says the nafs is a body distinct from blood.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون : هي جسم غير الدم .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r5.claim: Another view treats the nafs as an accident because it is not found to exist independently.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : هي عرض لأنا لا نجدها تقوم بنفسها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r6.speaker: كثير من الناس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r6.claim: Many people hold that the spirit is distinct from the nafs.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r6.anchor: فقال كثير من الناس : إن الروح شيء غير النفس .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r7.claim: Others say the spirit and nafs are one and the same.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل هما شيء واحد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r8.speaker: كثير من الناس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r8.claim: Many people say human souls and animal souls are separate kinds.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r8.anchor: قال كثير من الناس : إن نفوس بني آدم جنس ونفوس البهائم جنس آخر .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r9.speaker: آخرون
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r9.claim: Others say all souls are one kind.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r9.anchor: وزعم آخرون أن النفوس كلها جنس واحد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r10.speaker: القائلون بأنها من جنس واحد
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r10.claim: Those who classify human and animal souls as one kind say the angel of death takes the souls of all animals.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r10.anchor: والقائلون بأنها من جنس واحد يقولون إن موت جميع الحيوان يتولاه ملك الموت في قبض الأنفس .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r11.speaker: القائلون بأنها من جنسين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r11.claim: Those who classify them as two kinds say the angel of death takes human souls, while animals die when their own souls expire.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p594#2/r11.anchor: والقائلون بأنها من جنسين يقولون : إن ملك الموت يتولى بني آدم في ذلك . فأما [ جميع ] البهائم

NAHHAS:v3p293/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p293/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p293/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains yatawaffākum as completing and taking the full number of you all.
NAHHAS:v3p293/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هو من توفيه العدد أي يستوفي عددكم أجمعين

SAMIN-DURR:32:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:32:11/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:32:11/r2.anchor: وزيد بن علي على بنائه للفاعل.

ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r1.claim: يتوفاكم derives from completing a count: the angel takes every soul, like collecting all money owed.
ZAJJAJ:v4p205/r1.anchor: أنه يقبض أرواحكم أجمعين فلا ينقص واحد منكم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r2.claim: An angel appointed over each person takes the soul at death; the deceased remains in God's sight, and God will raise each person and bring them before Him under angelic custody.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r2.anchor: his soul is claimed by an angel who is deputed by God on every person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r3.claim: The return is to the one God, not to alleged deities or intercessors, who will not exist on that day; God alone judges everyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p142/r3.anchor: no one should remain in the misconception that when he dies he will be brought forth to his alleged deities and intercessors.

QIRAAT-ER:32:11:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:32:11:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:32:11:13#1/r1.claim: The active Form I means you yourselves return, unlike the standard passive you are returned, shifting agency to the subjects.
QIRAAT-ER:32:11:13#1/r1.anchor: Active voice Form I (tarjiʿūna): ""you [yourselves] return"" — vs. standard passive turjaʿūna

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r1.claim: قل is a reply to the deniers: tell them that the Angel of Death takes them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r1.anchor: يستوفي نفوسكم لا يترك منها شيئا من أجزائها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r2.claim: يتوفاكم means to take the souls in full, leaving no part behind, or to take every one of them so that none remains alive; the root sense is taking something completely.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r2.anchor: يستوفي نفوسكم لا يترك منها شيئا من أجزائها أولا يترك شيئا من جزئياتها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r3.claim: The author explains توفي through استيفاء, noting that the patterns تفعّل and استفعال often overlap in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r3.anchor: وأصل التوفي أخذ الشيء بتمامه وفسر بالإستيفاء لأن التفعل والإستفعال يلتقيان كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r4.claim: Death is attributed to the Angel of Death because he directly takes souls by God's command; being assigned to people means he takes their souls and knows their lifespans.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r4.anchor: ونسبة التوفي إلى ملك الموت بإعتبار أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام يباشر قبض الأنفس بأمره عزوجل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī reports that the Prophet visited a sick Anṣārī with the Angel of Death at his head; the angel said he is gentle with believers, visits every household five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito without God's order.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج إبن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : دخل رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r6.speaker: الطبراني وأبو نعيم وابن منده
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī, Abū Nuʿaym, and Ibn Mandah are said to transmit a similar report about the Angel of Death.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج نحوه الطبراني وأبو نعيم وإبن منده

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r7.claim: Calling God the one who takes souls attributes the act to Him as creator of human acts, with no creaturely agency beyond acquisition according to Ashʿarīs, or because the act occurs by God's permission and will.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r7.anchor: ونسبته إليه عزوجل في قوله سبحانه : ( الله يتوفى الأنفس ) بإعتبار أن أفعال العباد كلها مخلوقة له

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r8.claim: Taking souls is also attributed to messengers and angels because the Angel of Death has helpers who draw out the soul; he takes it when its departure is near.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r8.anchor: ونسبته إلى الرسل في قوله تعالى : ( توفته رسلنا ) وإلى الملائكة في قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r9.claim: Abū Umāma reports the Prophet saying that God assigned the Angel of Death to take souls, except martyrs at sea, whose souls God takes Himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p125#2/r9.anchor: أخرج إبن ماجه عن أبي أمامة قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول إن الله تعالى وكل ملك الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r1.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that separate angels take the souls of humans, jinn, devils, birds, wild animals, beasts, fish, and ants; the Angel of Death later takes angels' souls and then dies.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r1.anchor: أخرج إبن جوبير عن الضحاك عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : وكل ملك الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r2.claim: That report says God Himself takes the souls of martyrs at sea as an honor to them, rather than assigning them to the Angel of Death.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r2.anchor: وأما الشهداء في البحر فإن الله تعالى يلي قبض أرواحهم لا يكل ذلك إلى ملك الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r3.claim: The majority hold that one Angel of Death takes the souls of rational and nonrational creatures; he is called ʿAzrāʾīl, glossed as servant of God, and has helpers.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r3.anchor: والذي ذهب إليه الجمهور أن ملك الموت لمن يعقل وما لا يعقل من الحيوان واحد وهو عزرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r4.claim: The author leaves the soundness of al-Ḍaḥḥāk's report from Ibn ʿAbbās to God's knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r4.anchor: وخبر الضحاك عن إبن عباس الله تعالى أعلم بصحته

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r5.claim: The return to God is resurrection for judgment and recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r5.anchor: ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون 11 ( بالبعث للحساب والجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r6.claim: If the preceding context says they denied meeting God's angels at death and what follows it, mentioning the Angel of Death signals that they will meet him, and return to God means resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r6.anchor: لأنهم لما جحدوا لقاء ملائكة ربهم عند الموت وما يكون بعده ذكر لهم حديث توفي ملك الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r7.claim: Alternatively, the verse answers their denial of resurrection; death is mentioned because resurrection follows death, as a warning and as proof that the one able to cause death can restore life.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r7.anchor: وأما على ما قيل فوجه المناسبة أنهم أنهم لما أنكروا البعث والمعاد رد عليهم بما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r8.claim: The author calls it a weak interpretation that the verse rebuts a naturalistic account of death inferred from their phrase أئذا ضللنا في الأرض.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r8.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك لرد ما يشعر به كلامهم من أن الموت بمقتضى الطبيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r9.claim: The author calls still more remote the argument that because ʿAzrāʾīl extracts the soul from the body, the Creator can distinguish bodily parts mixed into earth; the soul's hidden relation was disputed even by rational people.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r9.anchor: وأبعد منه ما قيل في المناسبة : إن عزرائيل وهو عبد من عبيده تعالى إذا قدر على تخليص الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r10.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r10.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads ترجعون in the active voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p126/r10.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( ترجعون ) بالبناء للفاعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r1.claim: “He takes you” means that the angel takes your souls.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r1.anchor: {قل يتوفاكم} يقبض أرواحكم، {ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم} أي: وكل بقبض أرواحكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r2.claim: The angel appointed to take souls is identified as Azrael; “taking in full” means he takes every soul whose death has been decreed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r2.anchor: وهو عزرائيل، والتوفي استيفاء العدد، معناه أنه يقبض أرواحهم حتى لا يبقى أحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r3.claim: A report says the world is made for the Angel of Death like the palm of a hand, allowing him to take souls anywhere without difficulty; angels of mercy and punishment assist him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r3.anchor: وروي أن ملك الموت جعلت له الدنيا مثل راحة اليد يأخذ منها صاحبها ما أحب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says one stride of the Angel of Death spans the distance from east to west.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن خطوة ملك الموت ما بين المشرق والمغرب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r5.claim: Mujahid says the earth was made like a basin from which the angel can reach wherever he wishes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: جعلت له الأرض مثل طست يتناول منها حيث يشاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r6.claim: Another report places the Angel of Death on a ladder between heaven and earth: his helpers draw out a person’s soul, and he takes it when it reaches the throat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r6.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار: أن ملك الموت على معراج بين السماء والأرض فينزع أعوانه روح الإنسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r7.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r7.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan transmits from Muʿadh ibn Jabal that the Angel of Death carries a spear spanning east to west, inspects every face twice daily, and strikes the head of anyone whose term ends, announcing his visit to the army of the dead.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r7.anchor: وروى خالد بن معدان عن معاذ بن جبل قال: إن لملك الموت حربة تبلغ ما بين المشرق والمغرب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r8.claim: People return alive to God so that He may recompense them for their deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p302/r8.anchor: أي: تصيرون إليه أحياء فيجزيكم بأعمالكم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r1.claim: The angel takes all of your souls and leaves none of you behind; tafaʿʿala and istafʿala often converge in meaning, as in the paired verbs he cites.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r1.anchor: يستوفي نفوسكم لا يترك منها شيئا ولا يبقي منكم أحدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r2.claim: The Angel of Death is assigned to take people's souls and keep count of their appointed lifespans.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:11-12/r3.claim: People return to their Lord for judgment and recompense.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r1.claim: Because deniers think resurrection impossible after body parts mingle with earth, God points to their acknowledged example of souls being taken from bodies mixed among the earth's parts.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r1.anchor: وكان إنكارهم إنما هو بسبب اختلاط الأجزاء بالتراب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r2.claim: The Angel of Death takes each soul completely from its body after the body has mingled with soil throughout the lands, though people cannot distinguish its parts by ordinary means.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r2.anchor: بعد أن كانت مختلطة بجميع أجزاء البلدان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r3.claim: The passive وكّل leaves the agent unstated to emphasize the ease and divine power behind the task; the creator commissioned the Angel of Death, His servant, to carry it out.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r3.anchor: ببناء الفعل لما لم يسم فاعله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r4.claim: The body remains complete when the soul is removed, and soul-body mingling is closer than the body's mixing with soil; if a commissioned servant can do this, the Lord can distinguish every particle for resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r4.anchor: فإذا البدن ملقى لا روح في شيء منه وهو على حاله كاملا لا نقص في شيء منه يدعي الخلل بسببه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r5.claim: The unspoken next step is that God recreates them as they were at first; this resurrection is omitted because the context makes it clear.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r5.anchor: فحذفه كما هو عادة القرآن في حذف كل ما دل عليه السياق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r6.claim: They return to the Lord who first created and nurtured them, are raised together before Him, and receive recompense; like a king with servants, He does not leave wrongdoers unattended.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p54/r6.anchor: بأن يجازي كلا بما فعل , كما هو دأب الملوك مع عبيدهم

DURR-FULL:v6p543/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r1.claim: Qatada says the Angel of Death takes people at death with other angels assisting him.
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت} قال: ملك الموت يتوفاكم وله أعوان من الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v6p543/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r2.claim: Mujahid says the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, from which he takes souls wherever he wishes.
DURR-FULL:v6p543/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت} قال: حويت له الأرض فجعلت له مثل طست يتناول منها حيث يشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p336/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p336/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p336/r1.claim: The angel commissioned over people is charged with taking their souls; their return to their Lord is on the Day of Recompense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p336/r1.anchor: أي بقبض أرواحكم ﴿ ثم إلى ربكم ترجعون ﴾ يوم الجزاء

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r1.speaker: الكلبي
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r1.claim: Qatāda, Muqātil, and al-Kalbī say the angel of death has many helpers among the angels of mercy and punishment; “angel of death” then denotes the class.
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r1.anchor: والكلبي. وعلى هذا أراد بملك الموت الجنس، يدل عليه قوله: (توفته رسلنا)

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r2.claim: To reconcile the angel’s taking souls with God’s taking souls, God alone creates death, while the angel of death seizes spirits or directs his helpers; this is the strongest account.
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r2.anchor: قلنا: الله يخلق الموت ولا يقدر عليه أحد سواه، وملك الموت يقبض الأرواح، أو يأمر به أعوانه، وهذا هو الأوجه

JISHUMI:v8p5678/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r3.claim: Another account says God takes the souls and orders the angels to seize them; the author prefers the preceding explanation, in which the angel seizes the spirit on which life depends and life ceases.
JISHUMI:v8p5678/r3.anchor: وقيل: الله تعالى هو المتوفي وأمر الملائكة بالقبض، والأول أوجه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r10.claim: Taking a soul is taking it fully and leaving none, as in 39:42 and the command أخرجوا أنفسكم.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r10.anchor: والتوفي : استيفاء النفس وهي الروح . قال الله تعالى : { الله يتوفى الأنفس }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r11.claim: The root is illustrated by taking one’s due in full without reduction; paired forms such as تفعّل and استفعال can coincide in meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r11.anchor: من قولك : توفيت حقي من فلان ، واستوفيته إذا أخذته وافيا كاملا من غير نقصان .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r12.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r12.claim: Mujāhid says the earth was compressed for the angel of death like a platter, letting him reach wherever he wishes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r12.anchor: وعن مجاهد رضي الله عنه : حويت لملك الموت والأرض ، وجعلت له مثل الطست ، يتناول منها حيث يشاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r13.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r13.claim: Qatāda says the angel of death takes people with assistants from among the angels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r13.anchor: وعن قتادة : يتوفاهم ومعه أعوان من الملائكة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p516/r14.claim: Another account says the angel of death summons souls, they respond, and he orders his assistants to seize them.

MUJAHID:v2p510#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p510#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p510#2/r1.claim: Mujahid reports that the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, so he can reach wherever he wishes.
MUJAHID:v2p510#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ يتوفاكم ملك الموت ﴾ قال حويت له الأرض فجعلت له مثل الطست ينال

NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r1.claim: The commissioned Angel of Death takes all their souls; afterward they are raised and returned to their Lord for reckoning and recompense.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r1.anchor: يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذى وكل بقبض أرواحكم ثم ترجعون إلى ربكم بعد ذلك مبعوثين للحساب والجزاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r2.claim: Tawaffī means taking the soul completely, as one collects a full due; here the soul means the spirit.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r2.anchor: والتوفى استبفاء النفس وهى الروح أى يقبض أرواحكم أجمعين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, from which he takes souls wherever he wishes.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد حويت لملك الموت الأرض وجعلت له مثل الطست يتناول منها حيث يشاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r4.claim: Another account says the Angel of Death summons souls and they answer; he then orders assistants to seize them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r4.anchor: وقيل ملك الموت يدعو الأرواح فتجيبه ثم يأمر أعوانه بقبضها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r5.claim: God commands the whole process and creates creatures' acts, reconciling this verse with verses saying the messengers or God take souls.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p290#6/r5.anchor: والله تعالى هو الآمر لذلك كله وهو الخالق لأفعال المخلوقات وهذا وجه الجمع بين هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r1.claim: Because the preceding discussion mentioned their doubt about resurrection, this verse tells of their death and return to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r1.anchor: لما ذكر استبعادهم للبعث ذكر توفيهم وأنه يعيدهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r2.claim: Yatawaffākum derives from taking a count or thing in full: God takes the soul completely and then seizes it; the same verb can mean collecting one’s property in full.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r2.anchor: { يتوفاكم } من توفى العدد والشيء إذا استوفاه وقبضه جميعا.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r3.claim: The Angel of Death is named ʿAzrāʾīl, meaning Servant of God; the author refers to his earlier discussion in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r3.anchor: { ملك الموت } واسمه عزرائيل ومعناه عبد الله كما تقدم في «البقرة».

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r4.claim: The Angel of Death acts wholly by God’s command, creation, and origination.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r4.anchor: وتصرفه كله بأمر الله تعالى وبخلقه واختراعه.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentions a report that God takes the souls of animals without the Angel of Death, as though their life is simply extinguished.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r5.anchor: كأنه يعدم حياتها ذكره ابن عطية.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r6.claim: The author cites a contrary report that the Angel of Death takes the souls of all creatures, down to fleas and mosquitoes.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r6.anchor: قلت: وقد روي خلافه، وأن ملك الموت يتوفى أرواح جميع الخلائق حتى البرغوث والبعوضة.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r7.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r7.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad transmits from his father that the Prophet asked the Angel to treat a believing Anṣārī gently; the angel said he is gentle with every believer and inspects every household five times daily, yet cannot take even a mosquito’s soul without God’s order.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r7.anchor: روى جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال: " نظر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ملك الموت عند رأس رجل من الأنصار،

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r8.speaker: جعفر بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r8.claim: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAlī says he was told the Angel of Death inspects people at prayer times; al-Māwardī records this.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r8.anchor: قال جعفر بن علي: بلغني أنه يتصفحهم عند مواقيت الصلوات ذكره الماوردي.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r9.speaker: مالك بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r9.claim: Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī reports that Mālik, asked whether the Angel of Death takes flea souls, answered yes after asking whether fleas have souls, citing 39:42.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r9.anchor: فأطرق مالك طويلا ثم قال: ألها أنفس؟ قال: نعم. قال: ملك الموت يقبض أرواحها

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says human souls are likewise taken by the Angel, with a special honor in the Angel and other angels sharing the work; God created the Angel to extract souls and created a host to assist under his command.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية بعد ذكره الحديث: وكذلك الأمر في بني آدم، إلا أنه نوع شرف بتصرف ملك وملائكة معه في قبض أرواحهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi links the verse to passages describing angels taking disbelievers and God's messengers taking souls.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r1.anchor: ولو ترى إذ يتوفى الذين كفروا الملائكة [الأنفال: 50]، وقال تعالى: { توفته رسلنا }

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r2.claim: God is the true creator and agent of every act; He gives life, brings death, and takes souls, as other verses state.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r2.anchor: والبارىء خالق الكل، الفاعل حقيقة لكل فعل قال الله تعالى: { الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r3.claim: The Angel of Death takes souls directly, his assistants handle them, and God ultimately takes the spirit; the act is attributed to the angel because he is entrusted with its direct execution, as creation can be attributed to an angel.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r3.anchor: فملك الموت يقبض والأعوان يعالجون والله تعالى يزهق الروح. وهذا هو الجمع بين الآي والأحاديث

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r4.claim: Mujahid compares the world before the Angel of Death to a basin before a person, from which he takes wherever he wishes.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أن الدنيا بين يدي ملك الموت كالطست بين يدي الإنسان يأخذ من حيث شاء

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r5.claim: Qurtubi says the comparison of the world to a basin before the Angel of Death was also reported as a Prophetic narration; he gives no grading here.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r5.anchor: وقد روي هذا المعنى مرفوعا، وقد ذكرناه في كتاب التذكرة

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r6.claim: A report says the Angel of Death complained that people blame and curse him; God said He would make death appear to result from illnesses so people would speak well of him.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r6.anchor: وروي أن ملك الموت لما وكله الله تعالى بقبض الأرواح قال: رب جعلتني أذكر بسوء ويشتمني بنو آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r7.claim: Qurtubi says the Angel of Death summons souls, takes them, and hands them to the angels of mercy or punishment; he refers readers to his Tadhkira for details.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r7.anchor: وقد ذكرنا أنه يدعو الأرواح فتجيئه ويقبضها، ثم يسلمها إلى ملائكة الرحمة أو العذاب بما فيه شفاء

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r8.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r8.claim: Some scholars infer from the wording that agency is permissible, since the Angel of Death is appointed to take souls.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r8.anchor: استدل بهذه الآية بعض العلماء على جواز الوكالة من قوله: { وكل بكم } أي بقبض الأرواح

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects deriving ordinary legal agency from this wording alone: the purposes differ, just as God's commissioning a Messenger or commanding alms does not establish those analogies.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «وهذا أخذ من لفظه لا من معناه، ولو اطرد ذلك لقلنا في قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r10.claim: If the verse is read for its meaning, Ibn al-Arabi says it supports a judge appointing someone to seize a due right by force, without the debtor's act or consent.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:11#2/r10.anchor: أما إنه إذا لم يكن بد من المعاني فيقال: إن هذه الآية دليل على أن للقاضي أن يستنيب
